source_groups.label: Unnumbered Earl of Essex original May 1644 chart and historical identity
claims: unnumbered_heading
Robert Earle of Essex last setting forth into the west
An unnumbered original horoscope treats the Earl of Essex's expedition toward western England.
This appears after the prior numbered imprisonment chapter, not as a new numbered Lilly chapter.
chart_timestamp
munday 13 may 1644 12 29 PM
The printed chart is dated Monday 13 May 1644 at 12:29 PM.
Old Style calendar and historical clock have not been independently recast.
subject
Earle of Essex
The named target is parliamentary commander Robert, Earl of Essex.
An identifiable historical person, but no original prospective chart deposit authenticated.
figure_assignment
Aquarius ascending Sign
Lilly uses Aquarius ascending to represent Essex's external appearance.
Period physiognomic claim rather than historical evidence.
authorial_personal_description
comely forme of body
Lilly says Aquarius suits the Earl's comely physical appearance.
Retrospective interpretation; not blinded description.
figure_assignment
Saturn Mercury Venus ... mind
The source associates Saturn, Mercury and Venus with the commander's mind.
Astrological mental attribution, not independent personality study.
figure_assignment
Jupiter intercepted Pisces
Jupiter is given a role in Essex's qualities through rulership of an intercepted Pisces sign.
Precise house/glyph syntax needs specialist chart parity before computational use.

source_groups.label: Moon separating trine Saturn applying square Mars, assistance and journey
claims: condition
Moon separated from a trine of Saturn
Lilly reports Moon separating from trine to Saturn.
Exact period ephemeris positions not independently verified.
condition
applied square of Mars
The Moon applies to a square of Mars.
Requires motion and sequence, not merely an undirected square.
figure_assignment
Mars Lord Substance Assistants and Friends
Mars is taken as ruler of Essex's possessions, associates and support.
Several topical outcomes share one astrological significator.
figure_assignment
Mars Lord ninth journey
The same Mars signifies the ninth house, Essex's journey or march.
Ninth-house rule is separate from assistance and substance.
source_internal_forecast
slender success
Lilly forecasts only limited success for the western expedition.
Negative forecast with unspecified success threshold.
source_internal_forecast
much losse
He predicts substantial losses during the march.
No fixed numerical threshold or independently dated forecast.
condition
South Node ascendant
The south lunar node is cited as occupying the ascendant.
Additional adverse astronomical testimony.
source_internal_forecast
betrayed in his Counsels
Lilly predicts betrayal of Essex's plans or counsels.
No independently identified betrayer or precise operational episode.

source_groups.label: Saturn, Moon, Mercury, Fortune and Jupiter unfavorable geometry
claims: condition
Saturn Lord ascendant Peregrine
He calls Saturn the ascendant ruler and peregrine.
Essential dignity check not independently redone.
condition
Saturn in his Fall second
Saturn in detriment/fall in the second house is treated as adverse.
Original says fall; do not silently substitute technical detriment.
condition
Moon in her Detriment
Lilly explicitly treats Moon as in detriment.
Traditional essential-dignity framework.
condition
Part of Fortune disposed by Mercury
He reports the Part of Fortune disposited by Mercury.
A derived ruler, not a material outcome.
figure_assignment
Mercury Significator Enemies
Mercury is taken as a signifier of Essex's enemies.
No actually identified human enemy by this figure.
condition
Jupiter dexter square ascending degree
Jupiter is said to form a near-exact dexter square to the ascendant degree.
Dexter orientation/orb unverified.
method
I onely gave this Judgment
The adverse testimonies are summarized by Lilly as a judgment.
Author's alleged prior verbal pronouncement, no authenticated contemporaneous record.

source_groups.label: Detailed negative Essex expedition forecasts and patronage opposition
claims: source_internal_forecast
no successe from this imployment
Lilly says he predicted failure of the expedition.
No prospective frozen event definition.
source_internal_forecast
no honour by the Journey
He predicts no honor from the march.
Different endpoint from military loss.
source_internal_forecast
extreamly crossed by men of great power London
He anticipates opposition from powerful figures in London.
Claims about other people's intent are not independently demonstrated.
source_internal_forecast
pretended friendship
Lilly says some powerful opponents only pretended friendship.
Unverified hidden-motive prediction.
source_internal_forecast
betrayed wholly
He forecasts severe betrayal.
More intense wording than the earlier council-betrayal claim.
source_internal_forecast
danger to lose all
He warns that Essex might lose everything.
Risk statement rather than definite unconditional total loss.
authorial_evaluation
sorry unluckie time set forth
The astrologer expresses regret that the Earl departed at what he judged an unlucky moment.
Personal reaction, not a predicted outcome.
source_qualification
cum multis aliis
He alludes to additional predictions without specifying them.
Unspecified omitted forecasts must not be invented or scored.

source_groups.label: Author-reported early success and ridicule of his adverse judgment
claims: authorial_outcome_claim
prospered in the beginning
The author acknowledges Essex initially prospered.
Explicit temporary positive phase, contrary to an unqualified failure narrative.
authorial_reception_claim
daily men good quality authority jeered
He reports influential people ridiculed his negative prediction.
No identified critics or independent contemporary correspondence.
authorial_reception_claim
derided my former prediction
He says his earlier judgment was mocked.
Retrospective assertion that a prior prediction existed, not timestamped proof.
authorial_reception_claim
content to have been abused conditionally he better
He remarks he would have accepted being wrong if the Earl had succeeded.
Source rhetorical stance, not statistical evidence.

source_groups.label: September 1644 military news and separation of Army versus commander
claims: authorial_outcome_claim
eighth of September following came sad newes
Lilly says news of reverses reached him on September 8.
Reported receipt date not independently recorded as Lilly's notice.
authorial_outcome_claim
second of September this worthy man surrendered Ammunition
He claims that on September 2 the Earl's ammunition was surrendered to the King.
Independent historical account confirms Essex's **army** surrendered arms/ammunition on 2 Sep, while Essex personally escaped by sea 1 Sep; the two actors must not be merged.
authorial_outcome_claim
only Quarter for his Souldiers
Lilly reports the soldiers were granted quarter as surrender terms.
External registered-battlefield history confirms Parliamentary troops were allowed to march away after arms surrender.
authorial_outcome_claim
with some other Articles
He describes other capitulation conditions but leaves them unspecified.
Do not infer specific clauses.
authorial_accusation
which dishonourably performed
He claims the terms were later carried out dishonorably by royalists.
Contested partisan assertion not independently corroborated by this particular external check.
authorial_accusation
eternall shame royall Party
He condemns the Royalist side for supposed betrayal of articles.
Period political rhetoric, not a proven judgment.
external_historical_disposition
Essex personally escaped Sept 1
A separate modern historical authority documents that Essex himself escaped via sea on September 1 before the army's September 2 capitulation.
Corroboration of military outcome and factual distinction, NOT independent authentication of Lilly's earlier astrology forecast.
